# The leak matrix — verdict pairs per generated cell (self_host_leak_matrix_test.go).
#
# Format: <cell> <native-verdict> <selfhost-verdict> <note>
# Verdicts: clean (live_bytes 0), leak, error (did not compile), crash.
#
# This file IS the goal-2 RECLAIM gap list for the shapes the generator covers:
# a leak row is a known gap with its reason; flipping one to clean is progress
# and belongs to the change that earns it; a clean row going leak is a
# regression the gate reports. Regenerate measurements with
# FERN_LEAK_MATRIX_DUMP=1 — never hand-edit a verdict without a measured run.

enum_scalar__callarg__read                    clean  clean  the plan-routed escape gate no longer refuses a plain call arg (native parity: computeFreeEligible does not taint call args)
enum_scalar__callarg__stored_struct           clean  leak  matching DIRECTLY on a struct's enum-typed field access leaks the scrutinee: lower_stmt_match stores it into a fresh $mscrut scratch local that nothing ever releases, and the emitted main differs from the bound form by exactly one __fern_arr_dec (8 vs 9), the only differing call. Not the call taint rule (native is clean with findReturnsFreshBox disabled) and not the struct drop (the same struct with the field never read is clean 200/200, and __struct_drop counts match). Binding `var t: E = h.e;` first is clean. Only `match (h.e)` leaks, 3,960 B. WHICH site incurs the owed count — the field read or the literal's construction retain — is NOT established, and the fix's gate turns on it: releasing $mscrut unconditionally would over-free a bare-ident scrutinee. See docs/rc-log/2026-09-02-struct-enum-field-drop.md

tuple_mixed__callarg__read                    clean  clean  a tuple local passed to a READ-ONLY callee: the credit gate's own borrowability tier already admits it, so this row guards the tuple wave's routing rather than gaining from it — it must stay clean when the escape conjunct moves to the plan
tuple_mixed__structfield__local_store         clean  clean   the CALLER-LOCAL half of the counted-store question, and the instrument for the retain/drop pair: the struct literal storing a tuple field sits in the same body as the tuple local, so no interprocedural verdict is involved. Both sides now COUNT the store — the self-host retains it in lower_expr_struct_lit's tuple arm, releases it in emit_struct_tuple_field_drops (child walk under __fern_rc_is_unique, one box dec per owner), and forgives it in the TUPRC credit gate via rctuple_counted_field_share, all three gated on struct_has_deep_tuple_field so none can widen without the others. Knockouts measured: retain-only leaks harder (300/100), drop-only balances ONLY because the second owner's is_unique reads a freed header — a false green (docs/rc-log/2026-08-28-tuple-structfield-counted-store.md)
tuple_mixed__callarg__stored_struct           clean  clean   the callee KEEPS the tuple in a struct literal it returns — not a borrow, but a COUNTED store: the construction retains it and the holder's field drop gives it back, so the caller keeps its own deep free and the two net to one owner (rc 2 -> the struct sweep loop's box-only dec -> the rc-tuple loop's walk). Closed by the "TCNT:" tier in param_counted_of, admitted only when the callee's RESULT routes field reclaim — which Hold began doing only when the counted struct-field store gave a tuple field a releaser, so this row could not have flipped first. Both escape scans admit it, differently: expr_unsafe_for's call arm already reads the merged "CNT:" key, rctuple_esc_expr's reads only "TUPB:" and took the routing edit (knock it out and this returns to leak). An element handout in the callee still refuses the param (docs/rc-log/2026-08-28-tuple-callarg-counted-tier.md)
tuple_mixed__elemret__payload_refused         clean  clean  dup-at-extract landed: the return lowering retains `return src.1` (ret-tuple-elem) and TUPB/TUPRCS admit exactly that retained shape (tuple_elem_ret_dup — one predicate, two entry points). COUPLED with box_tier_only below: knockout of either half flips ONE of the two rows (retain-only -> that row leaks; grant-only -> this row underflows), which is the standing instrument
tuple_mixed__elemret__box_tier_only           clean  clean  call-producer flavor: element now arrives COUNTED (return retain) and the granted element kinds dec it in the caller's sweep before the box frees; final owner's is_arr sweep takes it to zero. COUPLED with payload_refused above — see its note

enum_rc_payload__fnscope__alias_match         clean  clean  the alias-bind forgiveness reaching the MATCH-CONSUMED credit path. #7687 taught body_unsafe_for_enumfield_alias (the exit-sweep scan) that a CONFINED alias is not an escape; consumed_rcpayload_enum_frees consults a second scan (name_escapes_outside_stmt_enumfield) that had not learned it, so a dead alias still denied the source its match-consumed free. Bisected before fixing: two matches on the source with NO alias are clean, and the alias alone denies the source, so the match is not the cause and the earlier diagnosis (match_arm_binds_rc_payload) was wrong. Same confinement proof (rcenum_alias_bind_sites_of), so the payload-out and returned-alias shapes stay refused (docs/rc-log/2026-08-28-enum-alias-match-consumed.md)
